questions.q: What does a symbol map do?
options: Places one mark at each individual location, sized and/or colored to encode a quantitative value
Shades an entire region's polygon based on a value
Only works with country-level data, never cities
Displays data as a bar chart overlaid on a map image
questions.explain: A symbol map places a mark (usually a circle) at each precise location, using size and/or color to represent magnitude at that point.

questions.q: What does a filled (choropleth) map do differently from a symbol map?
options: It colors in the entire polygon for each geographic area (state, county, country) rather than placing a point mark
It only works with live connections, never extracts
It can only show counts, never percentages
It requires a spatial file connection, unlike symbol maps
questions.explain: A filled map shades the whole region's shape based on a value, instead of marking individual point locations the way a symbol map does.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is a filled map showing raw counts (rather than a rate) a classic visualization trap?
options: Larger states/counties will visually dominate simply because they have more land area, even if the underlying rate is unremarkable
Filled maps physically cannot display counts, only percentages
Raw counts always render as a single flat color regardless of value
It has nothing to do with area — this isn't actually a concern
questions.explain: Because a filled map's visual weight is tied to a region's physical size, showing a raw count (rather than a rate) makes large regions look more significant regardless of the real underlying value.

questions.q: When should you choose a symbol map over a filled map?
options: When you care about individual, precise locations (specific stores, cities) and want to compare magnitude at a glance via circle size
Whenever you're showing a percentage or ratio
Whenever your geography is a large polygon like a country or state
Symbol maps should always be preferred; filled maps are never appropriate
questions.explain: Symbol maps suit precise point-level locations and magnitude comparisons; filled maps suit rates/ratios spread across whole regions.

questions.q: How do you switch between a symbol map and a filled map in Tableau?
options: Use the Marks card's mark-type dropdown to choose Map (filled) or a circle/shape option (symbol)
You must rebuild the entire worksheet from scratch — there's no way to switch
Only by changing the field's geographic role
Only by reconnecting to a different data source
questions.explain: Both map types share the same Marks card mark-type dropdown — switching between Map and a circle/shape mark toggles between filled and symbol maps.
